newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Israel officials due in Taiwan for trade promotion.
newsitem.headline: Israel officials due in Taiwan for trade promotion.

text.p: Taiwan and Israel are scheduled to hold a vice-ministerial meeting in December to promote trade ties between the two countries, which do not have diplomatic relations, a Taiwanese official said on Friday.

The meeting between Yehoshua Gleitman, director-general of Israel's Ministry of Industry and Trade, and Taiwan's vice economics minister Sheu Ke-sheng would focus on customs clearance and other general economic issues, said the official, from Taiwan's economics ministry.
About 10 Israeli officials and 15 Taiwanese officials would attend the meeting between December 4 and 6 in Taipei, the official at the International Cooperation Department said.
"This meeting is to promote more economic exchanges between the two sides, nothing political," the official said.
Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui, seeking to break out of a diplomatic isolation imposed by China, had planned to visit Israel during a trip to the Middle East in 1995.
But due to pressure from China, Lee only visited the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.
China has regarded Taiwan as a Chinese province not entitled to foreign ties since a civil war split the two in 1949.
Israel recognises Taiwan's political rival China, but Taiwan has said it wants stronger cooperation with Israel in aviation, information, telecommunication and biotechnology fields.
A 50-member Taiwanese trade delegation, including Taiwan's other vice economics minister Lee Shu-jeou, visited Israel in late April to promote trade ties.
In 1995, Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party approved an investment of US$7.1 million in an Israeli diamond company.
The party is also considering several joint-venture projects with Israeli partners, mostly in high technology industries and banking operations.
